title: Top 10 Essential Verbs in English, Part 2 (CEFR A0–A1)
dek: Part 2 of the ultimate beginner guide to high-frequency English verbs (A0–A1): do/make, speak/talk/say/tell, look/watch/see, listen/hear, must/have to, take/give/get, live, wait, understand, and ask/answer.

blocks.text: Welcome to Part 2 of our English verb guide for A0–A1 learners! In this edition, we explore 10 vital action, perception, and communication verbs.

items: **1. Do / Make:** Activity vs Creation (*I do my homework*, *I make breakfast*).
**2. Speak / Talk / Say / Tell:** Communication nuances (*I speak English*, *Let's talk*, *Say hi*, *Tell a secret*).
**3. Look / Watch / See:** Visual attention (*Look at this*, *Watch TV*, *I see a tree*).
**4. Listen / Hear:** Auditory focus vs involuntary hearing (*Listen to music*, *I hear a sound*).
**5. Must / Have to:** Expressing necessity (*I must study*, *We have to leave*).
**6. Take / Give / Get:** Physical and abstract exchange (*Take a coat*, *Give a present*, *Get a gift*).
**7. Live:** Dwelling and life (*I live in London*, *We live well*).
**8. Wait:** Patience and expectation (*Wait for the bus*, *Wait a minute*).
**9. Understand:** Comprehension (*I understand the lesson*, *I don't understand*).
**10. Ask / Answer & Want / Would like:** Questions and polite requests (*Ask a question*, *Answer the phone*, *I would like a coffee*).

• **Indo-European:** Features tense auxiliary verbs and person/number inflections.
• **Turkic Family (Tatar, Bashkir, Chuvash):** Agglutinative suffix structures expressing tense and person without separate helper verbs.
• **Kartvelian (Georgian):** Polypersonal verb agreement marking subject and indirect/direct objects.
